newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. spot resids hold despite crude, gas fall.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. spot resids hold despite crude, gas fall.

text.p: Most U.S. spot fuel oil prices, shrugging off weaker crude and gas markets, held relatively steady Wednesday in quiet trade, but few saw much upside, with demand still slack and gas competitive.

"We've come a long way and may have reached a bottom, but there's still no demand from Florida or the East Coast," said one cash trader, noting a $5-6 a barrel low sulphur slide from highs seen earlier this year.
In New York Harbour, physical one percent eased slightly to about $15 a barrel, while March and April one percent paper edged up slightly to $15.00-25, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour held steady at $17.00-25, but competitive East Coast city gate gas prices were likely to keep the grade on the defensive, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York again were stable.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was unchanged at $13.25, while three percent also was flat at $11.75-12.00.
But traders said firmer USG three percent paper, now in a steep carry to cash, might signal a near-term bottom for high sulphur. April was quoted on either side of $12.75.
A prompt USG 2.5 percent sale for 100,000 barrels was reported at $12.50.

New York city gate swing gas prices gained 10 cents Wednesday to $2.20/mmBtu, or about $13.86 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, gained more than five cents to the low-$1.90s/mmBtu, or $12.03 a barrel equivalent.
